definitions.explanation: A self-contained section of a larger musical work such as a symphony, sonata, or concerto, each with its own tempo, key, and character. Referred to by number (第一楽章, 第二楽章, etc.).

examples.japanese: ⟦{第一|だいいち}→第一：19377_daiichi⟧{楽章|がくしょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{始|はじ}まった→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{交響曲|こうきょうきょく}→交響曲：18025_koukyoukyoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{四|よん}→四：00767_yon⟧つ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{楽章|がくしょう}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: This symphony consists of four movements.

examples.japanese: {第三|だいさん}{楽章|がくしょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦テンポ→テンポ：04749_tenpo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{速|はや}すぎる⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{批評|ひひょう}→批評：03581_hihyou⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There was also criticism that the tempo of the third movement was too fast.

notes:
A music term referring to a distinct section of a larger composition such as a symphony, sonata, or concerto. Each {楽章|がくしょう} is a self-contained section with its own tempo, key, and character. Typically referred to by number: ⟦{第一|だいいち}→第一：19377_daiichi⟧{楽章|がくしょう}, {第二|だいに}{楽章|がくしょう}, etc.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{第|だい}→第〜：03960_dai⟧～{楽章|がくしょう}: ~th movement
- {楽章|がくしょう}⟦{間|かん}→〜間：28469_kan⟧: between movements
- {終|しゅう}{楽章|がくしょう}: final movement (also called ⟦{最終|さいしゅう}→最終：02820_saishuu⟧{楽章|がくしょう})

TYPICAL STRUCTURE (symphony):
- ⟦{第一|だいいち}→第一：19377_daiichi⟧{楽章|がくしょう}: usually fast (Allegro)
- {第二|だいに}{楽章|がくしょう}: usually slow (Adagio/Andante)
- {第三|だいさん}{楽章|がくしょう}: dance or scherzo
- {第四|だいよん}{楽章|がくしょう}: fast finale

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{楽曲|がっきょく}→楽曲：13182_gakkyoku⟧ — musical piece/composition (the whole work)
- {楽節|がくせつ} — musical phrase (smaller unit within a movement)
